dimensions.assessment: Affects hospitals with off-campus outpatient departments, group health plans, health insurance issuers, and patients receiving care at those locations.
dimensions.evidence: items and services furnished to an individual at an off-campus outpatient department of a provider

dimensions.assessment: Hospitals face claim rejections, prohibition on billing individuals, and civil monetary penalties of up to $5,500 per day for violations.
dimensions.evidence: not to exceed $5,500 per each such day

dimensions.assessment: Enforcement allows the Secretary of Labor to assess civil monetary penalties against hospitals, though federal budgetary totals are not stated.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary may assess a civil monetary penalty against a hospital for a violation

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA) to add new reporting, billing, and enforcement powers.
dimensions.evidence: amend the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 to require group health plans... to only pay claims

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent requirements taking effect for plan years beginning on or after January 1, 2027.
dimensions.evidence: take effect with respect to plan years beginning on or after January 1, 2027

missing_information: Aggregate financial estimates on the total volume of affected claims or expected federal penalty collections are absent.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill imposes new billing requirements and unique health identifier rules on hospitals operating off-campus outpatient departments, backed by group health plan payment restrictions and civil monetary penalties.
